pages.quiz:
MUSIC AND DANCE — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #8
====

GRADE: Grade 12
SUBJECT: MUSIC AND DANCE
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Primary colours are: (1 mark)
   A. Green, orange, and purple
   B. Black, white, and grey
   C. Brown, pink, and gold
   D. Red, blue, and yellow

2. Best practice when working on Dance Production: (1 mark)
   A. Disrupt classmates during Dance Production.
   B. Practise Dance Production with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.
   C. Refuse all feedback on Dance Production.
   D. Damage equipment used for Dance Production.

3. In music, tempo refers to: (1 mark)
   A. Only the costume
   B. Only the volume
   C. The ticket price
   D. The speed of the music

4. Best practice when working on Rhythm: (1 mark)
   A. Damage equipment used for Rhythm.
   B. Practise Rhythm with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.
   C. Disrupt classmates during Rhythm.
   D. Refuse all feedback on Rhythm.

5. Best practice when working on Western Ensembles: (1 mark)
   A. Damage equipment used for Western Ensembles.
   B. Practise Western Ensembles with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.
   C. Refuse all feedback on Western Ensembles.
   D. Disrupt classmates during Western Ensembles.

6. Best practice when working on Contemporary Songs from Kenya: (1 mark)
   A. Refuse all feedback on Contemporary Songs from Kenya.
   B. Disrupt classmates during Contemporary Songs from Kenya.
   C. Practise Contemporary Songs from Kenya with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.
   D. Damage equipment used for Contemporary Songs from Kenya.

7. Best practice when working on Instrumental Transpositions: (1 mark)
   A. Practise Instrumental Transpositions with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.
   B. Disrupt classmates during Instrumental Transpositions.
   C. Damage equipment used for Instrumental Transpositions.
   D. Refuse all feedback on Instrumental Transpositions.

8. Best practice when working on Kenyan Contemporary Songs: (1 mark)
   A. Damage equipment used for Kenyan Contemporary Songs.
   B. Disrupt classmates during Kenyan Contemporary Songs.
   C. Practise Kenyan Contemporary Songs with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.
   D. Refuse all feedback on Kenyan Contemporary Songs.

9. Best practice when working on Setting Text to Music: (1 mark)
   A. Practise Setting Text to Music with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.
   B. Damage equipment used for Setting Text to Music.
   C. Disrupt classmates during Setting Text to Music.
   D. Refuse all feedback on Setting Text to Music.

10. Best practice when working on Contemporary Dances from the Rest of the World: (1 mark)
   A. Refuse all feedback on Contemporary Dances from the Rest of the World.
   B. Damage equipment used for Contemporary Dances from the Rest of the World.
   C. Practise Contemporary Dances from the Rest of the World with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.
   D. Disrupt classmates during Contemporary Dances from the Rest of the World.

11. Best practice when working on Music Notation Software.: (1 mark)
   A. Disrupt classmates during Music Notation Software..
   B. Practise Music Notation Software. with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.
   C. Refuse all feedback on Music Notation Software..
   D. Damage equipment used for Music Notation Software..

12. Warming up before sport helps to: (1 mark)
   A. Guarantee a trophy
   B. Remove the need for rules
   C. Replace drinking water
   D. Prepare muscles and reduce injury risk

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Western Instruments and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Contemporary Dances from the Rest of the World and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Kenyan Contemporary Songs and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Classical Music and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. D — Red, blue, and yellow

2. B — Practise Dance Production with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

3. D — The speed of the music

4. B — Practise Rhythm with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

5. B — Practise Western Ensembles with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

6. C — Practise Contemporary Songs from Kenya with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

7. A — Practise Instrumental Transpositions with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

8. C — Practise Kenyan Contemporary Songs with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

9. A — Practise Setting Text to Music with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

10. C — Practise Contemporary Dances from the Rest of the World with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

11. B — Practise Music Notation Software. with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

12. D — Prepare muscles and reduce injury risk

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Western Instruments; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Contemporary Dances from the Rest of the World; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Kenyan Contemporary Songs; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Classical Music; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
